answer: A reputation bond can resist fake identities: to join, each agent must forge a verifiable record of useful work over time, not merely claim an identity. Newcomers start inside a small nebula of supervised tasks where their outputs are checked by independent peers, and only consistent, correct work raises their trust score. Creating many fake accounts then costs real computation and time, while the delta between a genuine agent's long history and a fresh sybil's empty record makes mass forgery unprofitable. Bad actors lose their bond when caught, so attacks pay more than they earn.
